I've saved the Q3 answers to `/work/answer.json`. Using the same method on Q2 gives all 10 of your reference values exactly.

| Question | Q3 result |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net sales | `smb`, 289,375,597원 |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 249 |
| c. Category with the highest net sales | `svc`, 251,013,953원 |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | `2025-08` |
| e. Customer with the largest total refunds | `u33@ex.com` |
| f. Customers with 2 or more paid orders | 238 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 684,190원 |
| h. Growth from August to September | -17.9% |

Matching the Q2 values took three choices about the data:
- **Time zone:** `ordered_at` is stored in UTC. I converted it to Korea time (UTC+9) before checking the quarter and month boundaries. Without this, a_net, c_net, g and h don't match.
- **Segment labels:** the same segment is written in different ways (`' consumer'`, `'Enterprise '`, `'SMB'`). I removed spaces and lowercased them before grouping.
- **Duplicate customers:** some emails, like `u33@ex.com`, appear on two customer IDs. I counted each email (spaces removed, lowercase) as one customer. Counting by ID gives b=278 and f=209 for Q2, which don't match.

The script is at `/work/scripts/an.py`.
